title: Clarify agent and model installation docs
description: Update the README installation and quickstart guidance so users can clearly choose (1) the target agent integration with --agent, such as --agent pi versus --agent claude, and (2) the independently selected model profile with --profile, such as --profile openai versus --profile claude. Include practical command examples for common combinations, explain auto-detection and when --agent must be explicit, list currently available/supported agent targets and model profiles (including inherit/none behavior), and make clear that agent choice controls file format/destination while profile choice controls rendered model aliases. Keep the README Install section and quickstart flow consistent with CLI behavior and current support gates.

title: Render pipeline checklist from orchestrator todos in pi-staffed overlay
description:
Layer B of the persona-checklist work. The orchestrator already decomposes the current prompt into persona dispatches and states the plan in prose; pi-staffed only observes subagent runs AFTER dispatch. Goal: have the orchestrator lay out the planned dispatches with the built-in todo tool, and extend the pi-staffed ledger to also observe todo tool calls/results (same event-driven model as subagent) so the runs overlay can project a pipeline checklist: each planned dispatch shown as pending -> running -> done, correlated with observed runs.

Constraints:
- Keep the extension read-only/observational. Do NOT make it a plan source. The todo tool is the source of truth; the extension only observes it.
- Do NOT give personas the todo tool. Personas are compact single-job workers; a per-persona task list invites over-decomposition and context bloat. Task-list ownership stays at the orchestrator.
- Reuse existing patterns: summarizeRequest already parses Composition/Effort lines out of the task string; a Plan/Checklist line convention is the lightest feed.
- Preserve honest async-launch semantics and standard-event-only observability.

Scope: ledger observes todo calls, overlay gains a pipeline-checklist view (or a section) correlating planned todos with runs. Tests in test/ledger.test.ts and test/render.test.ts.

title: Add structured persona contract checklist (Layer A)
description:
Layer A (follow-up, blocked by Layer B). Promote each persona's required output headings + Definition of done from prose into an explicit structured checklist block so the pi-staffed overlay can tick which required sections a persona actually returned (e.g. builder forgot ## Tests -> unchecked).

Current state: every agents/*.md has # Definition of done (one line) and # Output (always in this structure...) with required headings; personas.mjs validate() already enforces the output-contract heading exists. So the contract is already a build-time invariant, just not machine-readable per item.

Known wall: ledger.ts stores excerpt via summarizeContent (truncated summary), not full output. Full contract validation needs the full persona output, which the ledger does not keep. Likely options: (a) persona self-reports a ## Checklist block, (b) extension retains full output, (c) parse a Checklist: line convention like Composition:/Effort:. Prefer the lightest convention first.

Scope: define checklist block format, extend personas.mjs validate() to enforce it structurally, and have the overlay tick contract items per run. Do not give personas the todo tool.
